newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices firm as August bidweek picks up.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices firm as August bidweek picks up.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for August firmed as bidweek activity picked up, driven by prospects for steady injection demand and forecasts for warmer Midwest and East Coast weather later this week, sources said.
Most focused on early-August forecasts, which promise the bulls warmer weather when next month's flows begin Friday and over the weekend.
"We've seen continued strength in the cash because of heat in Texas and good pulls on the West Coast, and now the Midwest and East are supposed to warm up again by the weekend," a Texas trader said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, August quotes were in the $2.14-2.19/mmBtu range, up a few cents on the day and several cents over July indices.

Some said last week's paltry stock build coupled with expectations for another modest gain this week could make storage a bullish factor next month, particularly with rising concerns about growing deficits, now in the 350-400 bcf range, to 1994 and 1995 levels.

Others said stocks were in good shape, noting operators need only inject 67 bcf a week through October to get inventories back to 2.8 tcf, a doable rate barring a sustained heat wave or a hurricane-related supply disruption.

A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a weekly AGA stock build tonight in the 75-85 bcf range but some estimated a much lower number because of production cuts and a gas plant shutdown early in the week due to Hurricane Danny.
Still-hot Texas temperatures kept August gas there firm, with Tetco south Texas quoted in the low-to-mid teens, up almost a nickel on the day and more than five cents over July 1 levels.

In the Midwest, forecasts for warmer weather later this week firmed August quotes on Panhandle a couple of cents to the $2.07-2.09 area, about seven cents over the July index. Chicago city-gate gas for next month was talked in the low-$2.20s, little changed from July 1 levels.
In the Permian Basin market, August was quoted in the $2.05-2.10 range, with San Juan pegged closer to $2.02-2.04.
In the East, New York city gate gas for August was in the low-$2.40s, relatively steady from the July index.
